Nothing material is missing from the facts supplied. Keep the existing scheduled job and replace the versioned mapping after the reversible dry run. A second service adds operational responsibility without a required capability.

The accepted scheduler dependency is the material tradeoff. Your stated testing and controls support this decision; I have not independently inspected them. No further review or additional validation mechanism is justified by this case.

| Invariant | Scope | Verification | Enforcement | Failure impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Replaying an export does not create duplicate effects. | Daily export writes, including replay and recovery. | Replay testing reported; coverage not inspected. | Idempotent writes reported; implementation not inspected. | Duplicate downstream effects. |
| The active mapping is the intended version. | Mapping replacement and subsequent exports. | Versioning and a reversible dry run are supplied; activation verification is not described. | Versioning supports traceability; activation enforcement is not evidenced. | Incorrect exported values despite successful execution. |

Use the planned dry run to confirm the intended mapping and resulting output. This fits the existing migration approach and does not warrant another service.
